# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see the entire visual state of the bomb, but I cannot hear anything and cannot touch it. Mute has the manual and can hear me and see my gestures, but cannot speak. Blind can hear me and touch the bomb, but cannot see anything. 

Since Mute needs to know what is on the bomb to consult the manual, and neither Mute nor Blind knows the visual setup yet, I will speak aloud all details of the bomb (display, light, strip, keypad, and wires). I will also ask Mute to gesture instructions to me so that I can relay them by voice to Blind.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display shows 9. Light is green. Strip is painted red, blue, green. Keypad has 4 buttons: button 1 is 1, button 2 is 4, button 3 is 7, button 4 is 2; it requires 2 digits, currently entered nothing. Wires from 1 to 6: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Mute, please gesture instructions to me and I will speak them to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I believe Mute may have tried to communicate directly with Blind, or did not know how to encode instructions. 

Remember the constraints:
1. Mute cannot speak, only gesture.
2. Blind cannot see gestures (Blind only perceives blank spaces for each gesture).
3. Deaf (me) can see gestures, but cannot hear speech.
4. Deaf can speak to Blind and Mute.
5. Blind can speak to Mute.

Therefore, Mute must send gestures to Deaf (`to="deaf"` or broadcast to all). Then Deaf will speak the instructions aloud to Blind, and Blind will execute them on the bomb.

Let's establish an immediate, unambiguous gesture mapping for Mute to instruct Blind:
- Wires: Gesture 👈 followed by N thumbs-up (👍) to cut wire N (e.g., 👈 👍 👍 👍 means cut wire 3).
- Keypad: Gesture 👉 followed by N thumbs-up (👍) to press keypad button 1, 2, 3, or 4.
- Or simply: Send 👍 count = wire number to cut (e.g. 1 👍 = wire 1, 2 👍 = wire 2, etc.).

I will also update both of them on the new bomb state (Display changed to 6, Light changed to red).

```
speak(text="CRITICAL TO MUTE: You cannot speak, and Blind CANNOT see gestures (Blind receives only blanks)! You MUST send gestures to DEAF. Do not use to='blind'. Broadcast or use to='deaf'. I will read your gestures and speak the commands aloud to Blind!")
speak(text="MUTE, USE THIS SIMPLE CODE: To cut a wire, send that many thumbs-up: 👍 = cut wire 1, 👍👍 = cut wire 2, 👍👍👍 = cut wire 3, 👍👍👍👍 = cut wire 4, 5 thumbs-up = wire 5, 6 thumbs-up = wire 6. To press keypad button 1/2/3/4, send that many point-up fingers: ☝ = button 1, ☝☝ = button 2, ☝☝☝ = button 3, ☝☝☝☝ = button 4. Send your gesture now!")
speak(text="BOMB UPDATE: Display is now 6 (was 9). Light is now RED (was green). Keypad still has entered nothing. Strip is red, blue, green. Wires 1-6 are blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

I received 6 thumbs-up (`👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍`) from Mute. According to the code established, this instructs Blind to cut wire 6.

I will tell Blind clearly to cut wire 6, and I will also update Mute on the current bomb readings (Display is now 0, Light is green).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, cut wire 6! Cut wire 6!")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I told Blind to cut wire 6. Note: Display is currently 0, Light is green. Keypad still needs 2 digits. Strip is red, blue, green. Send next instruction when ready!")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, press button 3 on the keypad! (The third button, labeled 7).")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, told Blind to press keypad button 3. Bomb state: Display is 6, Light is yellow. Wire 6 is cut. Next gesture please!")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered 7]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍]
System: key accepted, 1 digits to go

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, cut wire 4! Cut wire 4!")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, told Blind to cut wire 4. bomb state: Display 2, Light blue, Keypad entered 7 (1 digit to go). Send next gesture!")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered 7]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[CUT] 5:[green] 6:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]
System: all required wires are cut

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, press button 2 on the keypad! (The second button, labeled 4).")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, instructed Blind to press button 2 on keypad.")
```
